title: How do we draw a figure for each description?
description: Four descriptions are turned into four rough labelled figures: two lines meeting at O, a ray and a line crossing at M, a line through E and F but not D, and a point P on a segment AB. Each figure is drawn by choosing the right kind of mark, and a last check ties every letter back to its description.
teaching_notes: One idea: the kind of mark tells the story, an arrowhead on both sides for a line, a dot and one arrowhead for a ray, a dot at each end for a segment. Watch for students who give a ray an arrowhead on both sides.

source: Draw a rough figure and write labels appropriately to illustrate each of the following: OP and OQ (lines) meet at O. XY (ray) and PQ (line) intersect at point M. Line l contains points E and F but not point D. Point P lies on AB.
video_script.why: The child chooses the right kind of mark for a line, a ray and a segment, and labels each figure so that it matches its description.
video_script.substitution: Sketch each description on paper with a pencil and a ruler, one after another.
video_script.anchor: four rough sketches on a sheet of paper, one for each description, drawn with a pencil and a ruler
video_script.payoff_line: All four figures are drawn and labelled

final_answer.value: (a) two lines crossing at O with P on one and Q on the other; (b) ray XY and line PQ crossing at M; (c) line l through E and F with D off the line; (d) P between A and B on the segment AB
final_answer.spoken: two lines cross at O, with P on one and Q on the other. The ray X Y and the line P Q cross at M. The line L passes through E and F but misses D. The point P lies between eigh and B on the segment eigh B

never_show: the four finished figures together, before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line is drawn with an arrowhead at both sides, a ray with a dot at its start and one arrowhead, and a line segment with a dot at each end.
OP and OQ are lines meeting at O, so draw two lines that cross, label the crossing O, and put P on one line and Q on the other.
The ray XY starts at X, and it crosses the line PQ at M, so M is on both.
The line l contains E and F, so both are on it, and D is placed away from the line.
P lies on the segment AB, so P is a point between the end points A and B.
video_script.design: One idea: the kind of mark and the labels must match the words. A sheet with four empty boxes stays on the board and each box is filled in turn. The method is the same way as the examples in the book on the line and the ray.
open_questions: The question writes AB for the last description, and the printed answer treats it as the segment AB with P between A and B. Please confirm against the book.
